stories.headline: Macron's Athens visit reframes EU defense as complementary to NATO, renews France-Greece strategic partnership
stories.summary: President Macron visited Athens on April 24–25 for a two-day summit with Prime Minister Mitsotakis, renewing a 2021 bilateral defense partnership that includes mutual assistance clauses. Macron used the occasion to deliver major speeches on European sovereignty, calling the current moment — with Trump, Putin, and Xi 'fiercely opposed to Europeans' — a unique opportunity for European assertion, while insisting EU defense was not an alternative to but a complement of NATO.

stories.headline: France announces fuel price subsidies and €6bn budget squeeze as Middle East war squeezes public finances
stories.summary: Prime Minister Lecornu announced new fuel relief measures for approximately three million low-income heavy drivers, fishermen, and farmers on April 21, simultaneously disclosing that the Middle East conflict would cost France at least €6 billion and ordering ministries to find €4 billion in additional spending cuts. The TotalEnergies CEO warned of possible fuel shortages if the Strait of Hormuz blockage continued; Macron sought to reassure the public from Athens that 'the situation is controlled.' Lecornu's popularity fell three points in a new poll.

stories.headline: RN courts business elite at Medef, CAC 40 dinners ahead of 2027 presidential campaign
stories.summary: RN president Jordan Bardella lunched with the Medef executive committee on April 20, following a secret dinner Marine Le Pen held with CAC 40 CEOs including Bernard Arnault and TotalEnergies CEO earlier in the month. Le Pen and Bardella also sent an open letter to business leaders proposing deregulation. The outreach sparked intense debate about far-right normalization in business circles; the Engie CEO called RN's energy plan 'a disaster.' Separately, reporting revealed RN faces repeated rejections from French banks seeking campaign financing.

stories.headline: Lecornu's Marseille visit: housing bill, narcotrafic meeting, and Armenian genocide commemoration
stories.summary: Prime Minister Lecornu spent two days in Marseille (April 23–24) announcing a housing reform bill to be presented to the Senate by summer, including a controversial reversal allowing energy-inefficient housing classified F and G to be rented again under conditions. He also had a high-security lunch with anti-narcotics activist Amine Kessaci, and commemorated the Armenian genocide while affirming France's military support for Armenia.

stories.headline: Jany Le Pen's undocumented Moroccan gardener expelled despite her intervention
stories.summary: The widow of Jean-Marie Le Pen, Jany Le Pen (age 93), visited the Nanterre immigration detention center on April 22 to plead for her Moroccan gardener of nine years, Hatim B., who was in irregular status. Despite her intervention and hiring of a lawyer, the Hauts-de-Seine prefect proceeded with expulsion on April 23. The episode, widely seen as ironic given the RN's immigration hardline, was covered across French media.

stories.headline: Health Data Hub switches from Microsoft to French cloud provider Scaleway
stories.summary: France's Health Data Hub formally selected Scaleway (Iliad subsidiary) on April 23 to replace Microsoft Azure as its cloud host for sensitive health data, ending years of controversy over US Cloud Act exposure. Migration is expected by early 2027. The EU Commission also separately selected a consortium including Scaleway and OVHcloud for a €180m sovereign cloud contract, prompting broader coverage on European digital sovereignty.

stories.headline: Government ministers' asset declarations published, revealing wealth disparities and conflict-of-interest concerns
stories.summary: The HATVP published wealth declarations for 30 members of the Lecornu government on April 20, showing a range from highly indebted (including Lecornu himself with a €559 overdraft alongside €443,000 in mortgage debt) to a minister worth €8.5 million. Nearly half of ministers were advised to recuse themselves from topics related to their personal holdings. Ecology minister Barbut was found to hold over €153,000 in shares including Airbus, BNP, and Sanofi.
